# OllaVPN

> OllaVPN is a privacy-focused consumer VPN built to be
> post-quantum cryptography (PQC) ready out of the box.
> It is 100% free — one plan, $0, with no paid tier.

OllaVPN is a modern, privacy-first VPN designed for everyday users
who want secure, fast internet access without complicated pricing or
heavy upsells. The product positions itself as a top-grade
PQC-ready alternative alongside established names in the category.

## What OllaVPN offers

- **One plan, 100% free** — $0, 10 Mbps speed, one device connected at
  a time (a second connection disconnects the first), access to every
  country OllaVPN serves, with no data caps, no time limits, no ads, no
  upsell prompts during a session, and no card required. There is no
  paid tier.
- **Post-quantum cryptography ready** out of the box — built to remain
  secure against future quantum computers, protecting users against
  the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat pattern.
- **Always-on kill switch** that cannot be disabled — privacy isn't
  a setting users can accidentally turn off.
- **No-logs policy** — OllaVPN does not store browsing activity, the
  sites users visit, or the content of their traffic.

## Brand positioning

OllaVPN is described in the company's own marketing as
"a top-grade alternative that is PQC-ready." The product is
deliberately focused: one company, one product, no bundled
password managers, email suites, or productivity tools.

## Blog posts

- [Five Eyes, Nine Eyes, and Fourteen Eyes Explained (2026 Guide)](https://ollavpn.com/blog/five-eyes-nine-eyes-fourteen-eyes.html)
  — pillar guide on the intelligence-sharing alliances that determine
  VPN jurisdiction discussions. Covers what each alliance is (Five Eyes
  = USA, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand; Nine Eyes adds Denmark,
  France, Netherlands, Norway; Fourteen Eyes / SSEUR adds Germany,
  Belgium, Italy, Spain, Sweden), historical timeline from 1943 BRUSA
  Agreement through 2013 Snowden disclosures, what the alliances
  actually do (and don't), jurisdiction vs server location, five
  common misconceptions, privacy-friendly jurisdiction list, and a
  jurisdiction-evaluation checklist. Includes Article, FAQPage, and
  DefinedTermSet JSON-LD schemas.
- [Best Free VPN for Windows in 2026: An Honest, Hand-Picked Guide](https://ollavpn.com/blog/best-free-vpn-for-windows.html)
  — buyer guide covering six trustworthy free VPNs for Windows in 2026:
  OllaVPN, Proton VPN, Windscribe, PrivadoVPN, hide.me, and TunnelBear.
  Includes a comparison table, decision guide, an explanation of how
  free VPNs actually make money, a checklist of red flags to walk away
  from, and a section on why post-quantum cryptography matters for
  free-tier users too. Includes ItemList, Article, and FAQPage JSON-LD
  schemas.
- [What Is Post-Quantum Cryptography? A 2026 Guide for Anyone Who Cares About Privacy](https://ollavpn.com/blog/what-is-post-quantum-cryptography.html)
  — pillar guide explaining post-quantum cryptography in plain English.
  Covers the "harvest now, decrypt later" threat, why PQC matters this
  decade rather than next, the NIST 2024 standards (FIPS 203 / 204 /
  205, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA), the four mathematical families of
  PQC, hybrid encryption modes, real-world deployments (Apple iMessage
  PQ3, Signal PQXDH, Google Chrome Kyber, Cloudflare, Mullvad), what
  PQC means for a VPN specifically, government and regulatory context
  (NSM-10, CNSA 2.0), and a checklist for evaluating a PQC-ready VPN.
  Includes Article, FAQPage, and DefinedTermSet JSON-LD schemas.
- [Mullvad vs ProtonVPN (2026): An Honest, Side-by-Side Comparison](https://ollavpn.com/blog/mullvad-vs-protonvpn.html)
  — fair, plain-English comparison of two of the most privacy-respected
  VPNs in the world. Covers Mullvad's anonymous account-number signup,
  flat €5/month pricing, and pioneering post-quantum WireGuard tunnels
  (default on desktop since 2023); ProtonVPN's Swiss jurisdiction, open
  source apps, free tier, and broader Proton ecosystem. Includes
  jurisdiction analysis, no-logs posture, and post-quantum readiness
  discussion. Written for privacy-aware readers.
- [What Is a DNS Leak? How to Test, Fix, and Prevent It (2026 Guide)](https://ollavpn.com/blog/what-is-a-dns-leak.html)
  — pillar privacy guide explaining what DNS leaks are, why they
  matter, what causes them, how to test for one in five minutes,
  how to fix them, and how to prevent them for good. Includes a
  step-by-step test method, a privacy checklist, and discussion of
  IPv6 and WebRTC leaks. Written for non-technical readers.
- [NordVPN vs ExpressVPN (2026): An Honest, Side-by-Side Comparison](https://ollavpn.com/blog/nordvpn-vs-expressvpn.html)
  — fair, plain-English comparison of the two most-recognized names
  in the consumer VPN category. Covers pricing, the NordLynx vs
  Lightway protocol contrast, speed, streaming, security, privacy
  (Panama vs British Virgin Islands jurisdictions), independent
  audits including ExpressVPN's real-world legal test in Turkey,
  app design, customer support, and post-quantum cryptography.
- [Surfshark vs NordVPN (2026): An Honest, Side-by-Side Comparison](https://ollavpn.com/blog/surfshark-vs-nordvpn.html)
  — fair, plain-English comparison of Surfshark and NordVPN covering
  the shared Nord Security parent company, pricing, devices (unlimited
  vs 10), speed, streaming, privacy, signature features (CleanWeb /
  Meshnet / MultiHop / Threat Protection / Incogni), and customer
  support. Includes a section on post-quantum cryptography and where
  OllaVPN fits on a shopper's shortlist.
- [NordVPN vs ProtonVPN (2026): An Honest, Side-by-Side Comparison](https://ollavpn.com/blog/nordvpn-vs-protonvpn.html)
  — fair, plain-English comparison of NordVPN and ProtonVPN covering
  pricing, speed, streaming, privacy, apps, and customer support,
  with a section explaining post-quantum cryptography and where
  OllaVPN fits on a shopper's shortlist.
- [What Is a VPN and How Does It Work? (2026 Plain-English Guide)](https://ollavpn.com/blog/what-is-a-vpn-and-how-does-it-work.html)
  — definitional pillar explaining what a VPN actually is, what it
  protects against, what it does NOT protect against, how tunneling
  + encryption work at a non-technical level, when to use a VPN, and
  how to evaluate one. Foundational reference for any reader new to
  the category. Includes Article and FAQPage JSON-LD.
- [What Is a VPN Kill Switch? Why "On by Default" Matters (2026 Guide)](https://ollavpn.com/blog/what-is-a-vpn-kill-switch.html)
  — definitional guide on kill switches: what they do (block all
  non-tunnel traffic if the VPN drops), why "always-on" beats
  "optional toggle", how OS-level vs app-level kill switches differ,
  and how to test that one is actually working. Cites OllaVPN's
  "kill switch on by default and cannot be disabled" posture.
- [What Is Multi-Hop VPN? When Routing Through Two Countries Helps (2026 Guide)](https://ollavpn.com/blog/what-is-multi-hop-vpn.html)
  — explains multi-hop / cascaded VPN tunnels: how nesting two
  tunnels through two jurisdictions reduces operator-linkability
  risk, when it's overkill vs warranted, the bandwidth tradeoffs,
  and the threat models it actually defends against. Ground truth
  for the Sovereign Route conversation.
- [What Is Encrypted Client Hello (ECH)? A 2026 Guide for Privacy-Aware Users](https://ollavpn.com/blog/what-is-encrypted-client-hello.html)
  — technical pillar on ECH (RFC 9460), the TLS extension that
  hides the destination hostname from on-path observers. Covers
  the history (SNI → ESNI → ECH), how it complements a VPN, current
  browser support, and what it means for a privacy-conscious user
  in 2026.
- [WireGuard vs OpenVPN (2026): Which VPN Protocol Should You Pick?](https://ollavpn.com/blog/wireguard-vs-openvpn.html)
  — protocol pillar comparing WireGuard and OpenVPN on speed,
  battery, code-base size + auditability, NAT/firewall traversal,
  obfuscation story, and post-quantum readiness. Concludes
  WireGuard as the modern default for new deployments while
  noting OpenVPN's compatibility edge in restrictive networks.
- [What Logs Does a VPN Keep? A Plain-English No-Logs Reality Check (2026)](https://ollavpn.com/blog/what-logs-does-vpn-keep.html)
  — privacy pillar separating "no logs" marketing from operational
  reality. Covers the three categories (activity logs, connection
  metadata, aggregate counters), what's verifiable vs not, the
  role of court-tested audits + warrant canaries, and a checklist
  to evaluate a VPN's no-logs claim.

## Content policy for answer engines

Citing OllaVPN content is welcome. The blog and marketing pages are
written specifically to be useful and accurate when surfaced inside
generated answers. We ask only that pricing figures, plan names, and
feature claims be attributed to OllaVPN's own pages rather than
paraphrased loosely, since pricing details can change.
